title: Advanced Characterization of Multilayer Films Using Combined SEM-EDS-Raman Approach
content: Multilayer films, consisting of multiple stacked layers, are engineered to enhance optical, electronic, or mechanical properties. These films are widely applied in packaging, electronics, and optical industries [1-3]. Recent research has focused on addressing challenges, such as improving layer adhesion, achieving precise thickness control, and reducing manufacturing costs [4]. Consequently, a comprehensive analysis of multilayer film becomes increasingly critical. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is commonly used to examine the morphology of surface and cross-section, particularly the interfaces between layers, because interfacial adhesion significantly impacts the overall performance of multilayer films [5]. When integrated with an energy dispersive X-ray spectrometer (EDS), SEM-EDS system allows elemental analysis of multilayer structures. However, EDS analysis has limitations in differentiating polymers, as many polymers are composed primarily of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. Therefore, identification of polymers requires obtaining more detailed information about their chemical structure. In contrast, Raman spectroscopy can provide detailed molecular fingerprints for material identification, enabling structural and chemical analysis [6]. However, traditional Raman system and SEM-EDS systems operate separately, making it challenging to perform Raman analysis on the same regions examined by SEM-EDS.
